BINDING SEAM (signatures and texts; §2.1 refers to this list). (0) NEW `rust/crates/storage/src/candidate_rows.rs` (declared `mod candidate_rows;` in `storage/src/lib.rs`; D-JSAH-STORAGE-READ-1 A): `pub struct SymbolRow { pub stable_key: String, pub name: String, pub qualified_name: Option<String>, pub kind: String, pub subtype: Option<String>, pub file: Option<String>, pub line: Option<i64>, pub signature: Option<String> }` and `impl StorageConnection { pub fn symbol_row_by_stable_key(&self, snapshot_uid: &str, stable_key: &str) -> Result<Option<SymbolRow>, StorageError> }` — ONE SQL query (`SELECT n.stable_key, n.name, n.qualified_name, n.kind, n.subtype, f.path, n.line_start, n.signature FROM nodes n LEFT JOIN files f ON n.file_uid = f.file_uid WHERE n.snapshot_uid = ? AND n.stable_key = ? LIMIT 1`); the read maps `line_start` 0 to `None` (the no-span sentinel is never a line — RG-REQ-012-L07, as the other storage reads do); `queries.rs` (`resolve_symbol`, `ResolvedSymbol`, `query_symbol_by_field`) is NOT touched. (1) NEW `rust/crates/daemon-runtime/src/dispatch_ambiguous_matches.rs` (declared `mod dispatch_ambiguous_matches;` in `daemon-runtime/src/lib.rs` — NOT as a child of `dispatch.rs`, which declares `explain_alias` via `#[path]` at :57-58; D-JSAH-PLACEMENT-1 with Correction 1): `pub(super) fn ambiguous_matches(storage: &StorageConnection, snapshot_uid: &str, keys: &[String]) -> serde_json::Value` — for each key IN RESOLVER ORDER, `storage.symbol_row_by_stable_key(snapshot_uid, key)` (seam (0)); a found row yields `{"stable_key": <key>, "qualified_name": <stored qualified_name, or null when None>, "name": <name>, "kind": "<kind>:<subtype>" (e.g. `SYMBOL:METHOD` — never a `:dupN` fragment; `<kind>` alone when subtype is None), "file": <file or null>, "line": <line or null>, "signature": <nodes.signature or null, verbatim — the renderer normalises whitespace>, "lookup": {"kind": "found"}}`; a key whose row is MISSING (`Ok(None)`) yields `{"stable_key": <key>, "qualified_name": null, "name": null, "kind": null, "file": null, "line": null, "signature": null, "lookup": {"kind": "missing"}}`; a key whose read FAILED (`Err(e)`) yields the same nulls with `"lookup": {"kind": "read-failed", "reason": <e.to_string()>}` and the error is still logged to the daemon's stderr — the two states are never folded together (D-JSAH-READ-STATE-1; RG-REQ-002-L04: a failed read renders unknown-with-reason); every candidate is listed, never dropped, never parsed from the key. `dispatch.rs` DELETES `parse_ambiguous_matches` (:228) and its four call sites (`handle_callers` :1375, `handle_callees` :1554, `handle_path` from :2795 and to :2834) call `ambiguous_matches(&storage, epoch.snapshot_uid(), &keys)`; `ErrorDetail::ambiguous_symbol(query, matches)` and its message `symbol '<query>' is ambiguous` are unchanged, so the JSON error code, message and the `query` field are byte-identical and `matches` gains fields (additive; `qualified_name` becomes the STORED qualified name). (2) NEW `rust/crates/rgr/src/commands/ambiguous_matches.rs` (declared in `commands/mod.rs`): `pub(crate) fn render_ambiguous_matches(cursor: Option<(&str, &str)>, data: &serde_json::Value) -> String` (D-JSAH-PLACEMENT-1 Correction 2: `Some((cursor_prefix, cursor_suffix))` when the failing command is known, `None` when it is not — the state is a type, never an empty-string sentinel) — renders, from `data.matches`, EXACTLY the byte form of SLICE_DOC §2.2 (column zero; the block below is that form with `\n` written out):

Candidates (<N>) — each matches '<query>'; pick one by its stable key:
  1. <file>:<line>  <qualified_name>  <kind>  <signature>
     → <cursor_prefix> <shell_quote_arg(stable_key)><cursor_suffix>
  2. …
hint: run one of the cursors above; a stable key names at most one symbol

A candidate whose `lookup.kind` is `missing` renders its row as `  <n>. ? — no stored row for this key in the snapshot read`; one whose `lookup.kind` is `read-failed` renders `  <n>. ? — store read failed: <reason>`; both are followed by their cursor line as usual, and the hint is unchanged (D-JSAH-READ-STATE-1). INCOMPLETE PAYLOAD (D-JSAH-INCOMPLETE-CURSOR-1): when a candidate's command cannot be formed — the `path` side is unknown because `data.query` is absent or equals neither argument, or the candidate has no `stable_key` — its row is still printed, NO `→` line follows it, and the final line is `hint: this listing is incomplete — <reasons>` instead of the run hint, where `<reasons>` lists EVERY applicable reason in this fixed order joined by `; ` (D-JSAH-INCOMPLETE-CURSOR-1 Correction 1): `the daemon did not say which path argument was ambiguous` (`data.query` absent), `the error's query matches neither path argument` (`data.query` present, equal to neither argument), `a candidate has no stable key` (a candidate without `stable_key`); `path_cursor_affixes` returns `None` for both unknown-side inputs, so the RENDERER chooses between reasons (i) and (ii) by reading `data.query` itself when `cursor` is `None` — absent → (i), present → (ii) — and reason (iii) by its per-candidate `stable_key` read; with an absent `data.query` the header is `Candidates (<N>) — pick one by its stable key:` (never `each matches '?'`). For a `found` row, `<file>:<line>` is `presentation::anchor(file, u64::try_from(line).ok())` (the payload's `line` is `i64`: a negative value fails the conversion and becomes `None`; `0` converts to `Some(0)` and `presentation::anchor` suppresses it — never `as u64`, never `:0`) — `<file>` alone when `line` is null (the storage read already maps the 0 sentinel to null) and `?` when `file` is null; `<qualified_name>` is the stored qualified name, the `name` when the qualified name is null, omitted when both are null (the suffix tier can list candidates with DIFFERENT qualified names — the column is what tells them apart); `<kind>` is the payload's `kind` (`SYMBOL:METHOD`) or omitted when null; the key is quoted with `presentation::shell_quote_arg` (`rust/crates/rgr/src/presentation/mod.rs:203`) — every stable key contains `#`, so it renders as `'<key>'`, and a key with an apostrophe — a REAL case: 1204 SYMBOL keys across the 29 retained v0.20.0 stores carry one, Rust lifetimes and generics in qualified names such as `ExtractionCtx<'a>.make_stable_key:SYMBOL:METHOD` (D-JSAH-CURSOR-1 Correction 2) — renders runnable as `'…'\''…'` (RG-REQ-012-L03); `<signature>` is the stored signature with ALL whitespace runs collapsed to one space (`split_whitespace().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" ")` — C++ stores the qualified declarator with its parameters, kafka stores multi-line parameter lists; the field is printed as its own column, never concatenated to the name) or omitted when null; the text `use qualified name` never appears. `handle_daemon_error` in `graph.rs` (:109-126) replaces the `Matches:` loop and the `hint: use qualified name for exact match` line with ONE call: `callers` → `render_ambiguous_matches(Some(("rmap callers", "")), data)`, `callees` → `Some(("rmap callees", ""))`, `path`: the ambiguous side is the one whose argument equals `data.query` — `from` is compared FIRST because dispatch resolves `from` before `to` (`handle_path` :2795 then :2834) — from-ambiguity → `Some(("rmap path", " " + shell_quote_arg(to)))`, to-ambiguity → `Some(("rmap path " + shell_quote_arg(from), ""))`, unknown side → `None`, the other argument quoted with the existing `presentation::shell_quote_arg` (`rust/crates/rgr/src/presentation/mod.rs:203`, the encoder `find` mirrors); `handle_daemon_error` gains one parameter `ambiguity_listing: Option<&dyn Fn(&serde_json::Value) -> String>` and each caller passes a closure that calls `render_ambiguous_matches` with its own `cursor` (`Some((prefix, suffix))` when the failing command is known, `None` when it is not); the `ambiguity_listing` parameter itself is `None` for a command that has no listing (two different `None`s with two owners: `ambiguity_listing: None` = no listing; `cursor: None` = a listing whose command cannot be formed); for `path` the closure derives the pair with `pub(crate) fn path_cursor_affixes(from: &str, to: &str, query: Option<&str>) -> Option<(String, String)>` — `None` when `query` is absent or equals neither argument — and passes it as the renderer's `cursor`; the renderer then prints no `→` line and the incomplete-listing hint — never a silent default to `from` or `to`, never an empty-prefix line; the error line `error: symbol '<q>' is ambiguous` stays first and unchanged. (3) `rust/crates/agent/src/explain/mod.rs` `classify_type_constructor_collision`: membership proof `container(ctor_qn) == type_qn` where `container` strips the LAST segment after the last `::` or the last `.`, whichever occurs later in the string (C++ `leveldb::Slice::Slice` → `leveldb::Slice`; Java `org.apache.kafka.clients.producer.KafkaProducer.<init>` → `org.apache.kafka.clients.producer.KafkaProducer`); `ConstructorHint.cursor` = the constructor candidate's `stable_key` (D-JSAH-CURSOR-1), `type_name` unchanged; the completeness rule (`count_symbol_definitions_by_name` equals the candidate count) and the one-type rule are unchanged. `NextAction.target` therefore carries the full stable key (raw cursor in JSON; RG-REQ-012-L03: a canonical cursor is untouched by the alias site). (4) `rust/crates/rgr/src/presentation/explain.rs` `render_related_cursors` (:316-333): the target is quoted with `presentation::shell_quote_arg` instead of literal single quotes (D-JSAH-CURSOR-1 Correction 1) — byte-identical `'<key>'` for every key without an apostrophe, runnable `'…'\''…'` for a key with one; its three tests' expected strings change from `explain 'Widget::Widget'` to stable-key cursors (names kept — they still describe singular/plural/omitted counting) and TWO new tests are added. `rust/crates/agent/tests/explain_symbol.rs:252` (`explain_bare_name_resolves_to_type_over_its_constructor`) is EXTENDED: its expectation `Some("Widget::Widget")` becomes the fake constructor's stable key (the test's name still describes what it asserts). TESTS (sixteen new, module-qualified names binding JSAH-C01; two existing tests extended): storage lib `candidate_rows::tests::row_by_stable_key_carries_signature_file_and_line`, `candidate_rows::tests::missing_key_is_none` and `candidate_rows::tests::zero_line_start_reads_as_none` (a row stored with `line_start` 0 reads back with `line: None`); daemon-runtime lib `dispatch_ambiguous_matches::tests::dup_key_match_carries_stable_key_stored_name_file_line_and_signature` (a `…:SYMBOL:METHOD:dup2` key against an in-memory store yields the seven fields with `kind` = `SYMBOL:METHOD`, `qualified_name` = the stored dotted name and `lookup.kind` = `found`), `dispatch_ambiguous_matches::tests::missing_row_is_listed_with_its_key_and_nulls` (`lookup.kind` = `missing`) and `dispatch_ambiguous_matches::tests::read_failure_is_marked_distinct_from_a_missing_row` (an in-memory store whose `nodes` table was dropped → `lookup.kind` = `read-failed` with a non-empty `reason`, the key kept, the other fields null — and NOT `missing`);
